Heisenberg's Uncertainty Principle in quantum mechanics can be understood by comparing it to taking a photograph of a fast-moving car. If you use a very fast shutter speed to freeze the car's exact position in the frame, the image is sharp, but you lose all sense of how fast it was going because there is no motion blur. Conversely, if you use a slow shutter speed to capture the blur and convey the car's speed, the car's precise location becomes smeared and unclear. Similarly, in quantum mechanics, the more precisely you measure a particle's position, the less precisely you can know its momentum, and vice versa.

The name of the planet humans live on is Earth.
